findings.message: PKCE is optional: an /authorize request without code_challenge yields a code that /token redeems for the GitHub token with no verifier and no client authentication. Authorize only checks the method `if codeChallenge != "" && codeChallengeMethod != "S256"`, so an empty challenge passes. ExchangeCode in session.go skips verification with `if sess.CodeChallenge != "" { verifyPKCE(...) }`. Token never checks client_id or a client secret. Anyone holding the internal code and redirect_uri gets the GitHub access_token back.

The client-supplied state is the session key and SaveSession overwrites any existing entry, so a second /authorize with the same state replaces an in-flight flow's redirect_uri and code_challenge. SaveSession does `s.sessions[state] = &Session{...}` with no check for an existing entry. Callback then looks up only by `state` (HasSession and CompleteCallback) and redirects to whatever `sess.RedirectURI` the most recent /authorize stored. Nothing binds the browser that started /authorize to the one that hits /callback (no cookie or server-generated nonce).

A second successful /callback for the same state mints another internal code without revoking the first. Both codes point at the shared Session, so the leftover code stays redeemable and can return a different (latest) access token. CompleteCallback assigns a new `code` and `s.codes[code] = sess` on every call, without removing an earlier sess.InternalCode. ExchangeCode does `delete(s.codes, code); delete(s.sessions, sess.State)`, but any other entries in s.codes still point to the same *Session, whose ExpiresAt is unchanged and whose AccessToken is still set.

Unauthenticated /authorize stores a session for every distinct state with no cap, so the map can grow without bound for the session TTL and exhaust the 256M container. Authorize sits on the public mux (`mux.HandleFunc("GET /authorize", ...)` in main.go). Each valid request calls `h.store.SaveSession(state, ...)` into an unbounded map, and the janitor only clears entries after ExpiresAt. The port is bound to 127.0.0.1, which limits who can reach it but does not bound the map.

If the user denies consent or GitHub returns error=, Callback answers with a bare 400 instead of redirecting the error to the client's redirect_uri, so the client's login hangs. Callback reads only `code` and `state` and returns `http.Error(w, "missing code or state", http.StatusBadRequest)` when code is empty. GitHub's `error`/`error_description` query parameters are never read or forwarded to sess.RedirectURI.

The new OAuth handler, session store and middleware ship with no tests, and CI has no Go job. The diff adds handler.go, session.go and middleware/auth.go but no *_test.go files. .github/workflows/lint-test.yml runs only `npm test`, shellcheck and bats, with no `go test` or `go vet`.

The default OAuth scope repo,user is broader than a PR-review service needs, and the raw token is handed to the MCP client. `GITHUB_OAUTH_SCOPES=${GITHUB_OAUTH_SCOPES:-repo,user}` here and the matching default in main.go loadConfig. ValidateToken only needs `/user` (read:user would do), and Token returns the raw GitHub `access_token` to the caller.

The validated-token cache keeps accepting a revoked token for up to TOKEN_CACHE_TTL_MIN, and the middleware accepts any valid GitHub token, not only ones this façade issued. ValidateToken returns early on `h.store.LookupToken(token)` without contacting GitHub. middleware.Auth accepts any token for which ValidateToken returns a login, and there is no user allowlist or token-origin check.

The Token doc comment says the client's client_id is validated by GitHub, but /token never reads client_id. Token reads only grant_type, code, redirect_uri and code_verifier. exchangeGitHubCode sends `h.cfg.GitHubClientID` from config, not anything the MCP client presented.

SESSION_TTL_MIN and TOKEN_CACHE_TTL_MIN accept zero or negative values, and a zero session TTL silently breaks login. getEnvInt returns any value that strconv.Atoi parses. main passes `time.Duration(cfg.sessionTTLMin) * time.Minute` to NewStore with no lower bound.

Callback re-reads the session through a separate lookupByCode lock acquisition instead of having CompleteCallback return it, and lookupByCode lives in handler.go. `sess := h.store.lookupByCode(internalCode)` runs after CompleteCallback has released s.mu, and the comments around it say it is a workaround. lookupByCode is defined on *Store in handler.go rather than in session.go.

Base images use mutable tags, not digests, and the Go 1.24 builder differs from the repo's 1.26 builder. `FROM golang:1.24-alpine AS builder` and `FROM gcr.io/distroless/static-debian12:nonroot` have no @sha256 pin. Dockerfile.github-mcp-server line 18 uses `golang:1.26-bookworm`.

The compose comment says health is validated host-side, but no host script checks this service. Without GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET the container crash-loops, and the new variables are missing from .env.template. A search finds no reference to copilot-review or port 8083 in scripts/health-check.sh. mustEnv calls os.Exit(1) when GITHUB_CLIENT_ID is empty. .env.template lists only GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, GITHUB_MCP_* and LOG_LEVEL.

Changing COPILOT_REVIEW_MCP_PORT moves the listener but BASE_URL stays at :8083, so discovery and the GitHub callback URL point at the wrong port. `MCP_PORT=${COPILOT_REVIEW_MCP_PORT:-8083}` follows the variable, but `BASE_URL=${BASE_URL:-http://localhost:8083}` is hard-coded. NewHandler builds the `/callback` redirect and the Discovery endpoints from BaseURL.
